explainer.heading: A routine with only a sealing step is half a routine
body: A moisturiser is thick, and its job is to hold water in and form a layer on the surface. That job matters — but it is the sealing step, not the step that gets anything in.
A serum is thinner, so it is the step that carries actives first. This bottle uses Liposome technology, and the ingredient table states each percentage rather than hiding them behind one trade name.
Which makes order as important as the product itself: serum first, cream after. Reverse it and the cream has already closed the route, and the serum you just paid for stays outside.

blocks.heading: Who this serum suits — and when it doesn’t
blocks.intro: We are a reseller. Selling the wrong thing to the wrong person means you give up after a few weeks — a loss on both sides. So the cases this bottle can’t help with, we tell you up front.

items.label: Thin skin that has flaked on retinol

image.alt: Close-up of thin, sensitive skin with slight redness

items.body: This is who the bottle was formulated for: no retinoids and no drying alcohol, so there is no peeling phase to sit through. Still patch-test on your neck and watch for 30–45 minutes before the first use.

items.label: Patchy or mixed melasma

image.alt: Close-up of mixed melasma, with lighter and darker brown areas on the cheek

items.body: What the 1000ppm 4-butylresorcinol is aimed at. The serum gets actives in; a cream has to seal them afterwards. If the pigment is marked and you want faster progress, the combo comes with that cream step.
items.fitNote: A fit — seal it with a cream

items.label: Skin after laser or microneedling

image.alt: Close-up of skin recovering after a cosmetic procedure

items.body: The manufacturer positions the product for this skin too. But post-procedure skin is a medical situation: ask the doctor who performed your procedure before adding any product.

items.label: Marks left after breakouts

image.alt: Close-up of skin with several brown marks left after acne

items.body: The serum goes on the whole face and helps soften areas of uneven pigmentation in general. If what you have is mostly individual post-acne marks, Mocha’s spot gel for dark marks is the better tool.
items.fitNote: The spot gel is a better fit

items.label: Irritated, red or freshly peeled skin
items.body: Let your skin barrier settle first. Adding actives now is the surest way to make it react harder. If irritation starts while you are using it, stop.

items.label: A dark patch that spreads or changes fast
items.body: A dark area that grows quickly, changes colour or shape, is raised, itches or bleeds needs a dermatologist first. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, ask your doctor before using the serum as well.

blocks.caption: Close-ups illustrating each skin condition (the brand's own image library) — not before-and-after photos of the product. Not sure which group your skin falls into? Send us a photo on Zalo and an adviser will take a look before you order.

blocks.eyebrow: Where it sits in the day
blocks.heading: Straight after cleansing, morning and night
blocks.intro: No need to change your routine. Just put it in the right place — and in the right order relative to your cream.

steps.label: Smart First Care serum
steps.note: Two or three pumps, patted in. Let it dry before the next step.

steps.label: Sunscreen
steps.note: Skip this and pigment returns whatever you used before it.

steps.label: Remove make-up and cleanse
steps.note: Actives land on residue if any is left.

steps.label: Moisturiser
steps.note: The sealing step. Apply once the serum is fully dry.

blocks.footnote: An airless pump bottle: no air gets in and each press gives the same dose, so there is nothing to judge by eye. Patch test on the neck and watch for 30–45 minutes before the first full use.

blocks.heading: Three steps, morning and night
blocks.intro: The order below is taken from the instructions supplied with the product.

items.heading: Cleanse
items.body: Wash and dry your face before applying the serum.

items.heading: One or two presses for the whole face
items.body: Spread evenly and pat it in. The pump gives the same dose each time, so you do not take more than you need.

items.heading: Seal it with the cream step
items.body: The serum opens the way; apply the cream straight after to keep the actives on the skin.

blocks.footnote: Sunscreen in the morning is not optional. Serum on its own, with no sun protection, lets pigmentation return whatever product you use.

Serum first, cream second. The serum is lighter and opens the way; the cream seals it in. The other way round, the cream blocks the serum.

items.q: How long does one bottle last?
items.a: 30ml, one or two presses for the whole face, morning and night. How long it lasts depends on how much you take — the airless pump keeps the dose consistent between uses.

items.q: Can I use it after laser or microneedling?
items.a: The manufacturer positions the product for skin that has been through those procedures. Even so, post-procedure skin is a medical situation: ask the doctor who performed it before adding any product.
Keep away from heat and direct sunlight, close the lid after use, keep out of reach of children. Avoid contact with the eyes; if it gets in, rinse immediately with clean water.
